The frontline team and the first people users turn to when something breaks:
Password resets, account unlocks, basic access issues
Email, Teams, and connectivity troubleshooting
Printer, hardware, and common software issues
Ticket logging, documentation, and escalation
🎯 Their mission: Get users back up and running with minimal downtime.

The specialists who dive deeper when issues go beyond the basics:
Handling escalated tickets from L1
Managing AD users, groups, and permissions
Software installs, patches, and configurations
Advanced troubleshooting using logs and diagnostic tools
🎯 Their mission: Resolve complex issues and prevent them from coming back.

The architects and guardians of the organization’s IT backbone:
Managing servers, networks, cloud, and security
Designing system architecture, upgrades, and compliance
Root‑cause analysis for major incidents
Performance tuning, automation, and long‑term improvements
🎯 Their mission: Keep systems stable, secure, and ready for the future.

📍The Technical Blueprint for Sustainable Business Growth
In today's competitive landscape, simply "doing more" isn't a strategy, it's a path to burnout. Sustainable, accelerated business growth hinges on a technical understanding and rigorous application of core frameworks, data analysis, and strategic optimization.
Here is a technical blueprint focusing on 2(Two) critical pillars for scaling your enterprise:
1. Product-Market Fit (PMF) Deep Dive
Scaling prematurely, before solid PMF is established, is a common growth killer.
A. The Value Proposition Canvas
Ensure your product's "Gain Creators" and "Pain Relievers" perfectly align with your target customer's "Pains" and "Gains." Document your Unique Selling Proposition (USP) as a testable hypothesis.
B. Quantifying Product-Market Fit
Use the Sean Ellis Test (asking users how they would feel if they could no longer use your product). A score of 40% or more responding "very disappointed" is a strong, technical benchmark for solid PMF.
C. Iterative Development & Scaling
Adopt a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) mindset for all new features. Implement a continuous deployment/integration (CI/CD) pipeline to allow for rapid, data-informed iteration based on user telemetry.
💥 Key Framework: Use the Build-Measure-Learn loop (from the Lean Startup methodology) to manage technical risk and ensure development efforts directly impact customer value.
2. Financial Modeling and Operational Scaling
Growth is meaningless if the unit economics don't support it.
A. Unit Economics Analysis
Every business must prove that the revenue derived from a single unit (customer, subscription, transaction) outweighs the cost to acquire and serve it.
💥Metric 1: Unit Profitability (LTV): Maximize this through effective pricing and upselling/cross-selling.
💥Metric 2: Contribution Margin: Calculate the revenue remaining after subtracting variable costs (COGS, commissions, variable hosting costs). Focus operational efforts on increasing this margin percentage.
B. Operational Leverage
Growth requires infrastructure that can handle increased demand without a proportional increase in fixed costs. This is operational leverage.
💥Automation: Automate repetitive, low-value tasks in sales, marketing, and customer support (e.g., using CRM workflows, chatbots).
💥Scalable Architecture: For tech companies, this means cloud-native, microservices-based architecture that can handle sudden spikes in traffic (spiky load) without failure or high marginal cost.
📍 Conclusion
The Growth Mindset: Sustainable business growth is not about random hacks, it's about Systematic Optimization. Implement a culture where every team (Sales, Marketing, Product) tracks its own set of North Star Metrics and uses real-time data to inform daily decisions.

Credits to Kevin Box 🛡️. Follow them for valuable insights.
Original post below:
======
Your boss will impact your mental health more than your therapist.
Working for the wrong leader will quietly wreck your confidence, career, and self-worth.
Gallup found 70% of employee engagement traces directly back to one thing: the Manager.
Pick wrong, and you’re stuck in survival mode.
Choose right, and you grow faster than you imagined.
The difference starts with language.
Here are 10 things toxic bosses say—compared to great leaders:
1/ Ownership
↳ “Figure it out. This is not my problem.”
↳ “Let’s work through this together.”
2/ Collaboration
↳ “Do what I say. Don’t ask questions.”
↳ “I value your input. Let’s discuss.”
3/ Support
↳ “That’s a YOU problem.”
↳ “How can I support you?”
4/ Time Crunch
↳ “I don’t have time for this.”
↳ “Let’s prioritize and find a solution.”
5/ Appreciation
↳ “You’re lucky to have a job.”
↳ “I appreciate your contributions.”
6/ Problem-Solving
↳ “Fix it, or I’ll find someone who can.”
↳ “Let’s troubleshoot this together.”
7/ Empathy
↳ “I don’t care how you feel.”
↳ “Your well-being matters to me.”
8/ Accountability
↳ “That’s your fault, not mine.”
↳ “Let’s own this and grow from it.”
9/ Recognition
↳ “Just be grateful you’re here.”
↳ “I want you to feel valued.”
10/ Innovation
↳ “I don’t pay you to think.”
↳ “Your ideas help us all win.”
What would you add to the list? Tell us in the comments.

Two creators commanded 43% of all views on Nigeria's digital skit-maker leaderboard in Q2 2026.
Our research team at Dataleum tracked every major Instagram creator this past quarter, analyzing views, likes, comments, and growth, so the industry doesn't have to guess who's actually winning.
The Top Performers
🥇 Top Male Creator: Folagade Banks. 88.8M views, 5M likes, 512K comments. Second consecutive quarter at the top, up 16.8% from Q1.
🥇 Top Female Creator: Maryam Apaokagi (Taaooma). 39.5M views, 2.5M likes, 104.7K comments. Also holding #1 for the second straight quarter, despite a dip from her 49.4M Q1 peak.
The Shift: Quality Over Volume
The real story sits just below the top spots. Sydney Talker more than doubled his views, from 34.9M to 79.4M, with just 12 skits. That 127% surge moved him from 4th to 2nd. Dezny climbed from 10th to 3rd with only 18 skits. Production quality and strategic timing are starting to outperform raw volume.
The Engagement Paradox
Total industry views hit 389.5M, up 21% from Q1. In the same period, likes dropped 3.4% and comments fell 12.3%. Nigerians are watching more skits than ever. They're just getting more selective about how they engage.
This is the kind of pattern you only catch through structured quarterly analysis, not headlines. It's the same rigor we apply to help organizations understand their own audiences and markets at Dataleum Intelligence.
